correctness.rationale: The Laurent-polynomial constant-term representation gives the digit exclusion and a uniform sparse-block multiplication congruence. The multiplier D_(2*3^(k-1)) is 7 mod 9 and hence generates every principal unit mod 3^k. Two explicit Legendre-leading-coefficient seeds produce both unit signs at every positive valuation. All cases including zero and k=1 are addressed; the attached executable independently checks finite boundary and example cases, not the unbounded quantifiers.

originality.rationale: Deutsch–Sagan Theorem 5.15 gives only mod-three digit classification; Sun 2010 emphasizes prime-level Delannoy sum congruences; Krattenthaler–Müller Section 13 supplies generating-function congruence algorithms at individual 3-powers; Alekseyev et al. 2025 give valuations rather than all first-unit digits or the 3-adic value image. No exact all-power two-ball image statement was found in the targeted published-finding corpus and primary-literature comparisons. The Sun full text could not be materially inspected and unseen equivalents remain possible. OEIS A088917 and A358360 address mod-three digits and valuations, not higher-power unit images.

value.rationale: Classifying a classical sequence’s entire 3-adic range is a natural arithmetic invariant, finer than its mod-three digit criterion and its valuation spectrum. The exact all-exponent residue count and Haar measure follow from a structural multiplicative sparse-block theorem and complementary valuation seeds, not from arbitrary finite enumeration.
